title: ShotSpotter Finds the Scene, NIBIN Finds the Story: Lancaster PD's Playbook, Part Two
summary: See how Lancaster PD uses ShotSpotter gunshot detection and NIBIN ballistic matching to build cases and connect gunfire across jurisdictions.
body_markdown:
Almost five months to the day after Lancaster's first ShotSpotter arrest, a second alert came in from the same general area. Not the same address. The same individual. This time, he had been shot. Seven times. Twenty-four rounds had been fired in total.


Officers arrived to find him in a car, attempting to leave the scene. The officers pulled him from the vehicle and applied two tourniquets on site before EMS arrived. According to the emergency room doctor who treated him, he would not have survived the drive to the hospital without that intervention. As Bowling stated, the same individual was not only the first arrest under the program, but also its first life saved.


The math behind that outcome is worth sitting with. ShotSpotter alerts reach an officer's phone in roughly 35 to 45 seconds after the first shot is fired. That single detail, more than any case study, explains why Lancaster’s ShotSpotter program makes an impact. The officer who arrived didn't have an address from a caller straining to remember which street the shots came from. He had a location already loaded on his phone before he pulled up.
